title: GoCardless completes FCA AI Live Testing as research finds 44% of Brits say AI providers should put payment mistakes right
summary: GoCardless, a Mollie company, has completed the second cohort of the FCA’s AI Live Testing (AILT) programme and released new research which points to where payer confidence needs to be built for agentic commerce to take off
body_markdown:
Findings follow the UK’s first agentic account-to-account payment, taken through a checkout GoCardless developed in the programme


LONDON, 24 November 2026:


GoCardless, a Mollie company, has completed the second cohort of the FCA’s AI Live Testing (AILT) programme and released new research which points to where payer confidence needs to be built for agentic commerce to take off.


In the survey of 2,184 UK adults, conducted by YouGov on behalf of GoCardless:


-


36% worry about fraud, hacking or their payment details being stolen if an AI assistant made a payment for them, the most common concern


-


34% say the area is not regulated well enough yet


-


32% would not know who would be responsible if something went wrong


-


30% would not know if they would get their money back


The results point to where confidence needs to be built before consumers let AI assistants pay.


44% of respondents believe that if an AI assistant makes a payment mistake, such as paying the wrong amount or the wrong business, the company that provides the AI agent should be responsible for putting it right. Meanwhile, 22% believe the payer should be accountable because they granted permission.


AI-enabled shopping is already commonplace


AI assistants already play a part earlier in the shopping process. In the past three months, 24% of UK adults have used one to research a product and 7% have bought something because it was recommended by an AI assistant. However, only 13% say they are likely to let AI make a payment for them in the next 12 months. Clear demographic splits emerge: the figure increases to 22% for those in London, and 20% for those aged 18-24 compared to just 7% for those over 55.


Payment was the focus of GoCardless’s work in the AILT, the FCA programme in which successful applicants test AI systems in real-world conditions, with regulatory support and oversight. GoCardless developed its agentic checkout through rounds of user testing and feedback from businesses. In September, it took the UK’s first agentic account-to-account payment, collecting a recurring donation for the charity Trussell, and in October it expanded the checkout to one-off agentic payments.


Hiroki Takeuchi, co-founder and CEO of GoCardless, said:


“Our research indicates that AI is already embedded in how many people shop, but paying is where they pause.Taking part in the AILT let us put a live agentic checkout in front of real payers. That experience will help lay the foundations of agentic commerce across the market. It’s an exciting start but for AI-driven payments to become widely adopted, an open trust framework is essential. It needs the whole ecosystem of industry, regulators and policymakers behind it and we’re proud to play our part.” To try GoCardless’ agentic checkout, visit[gocardless.com/checkout/agentic-commerce](https://gocardless.com/checkout/agentic-commerce) .


Notes to editors


For more information, contactpress@gocardless.com


All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. Total sample size was 2,184 adults. Fieldwork was undertaken between 19 and 20 November 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all UK adults (aged 18+).
